title: Signals plugin registry entry
description: One registry entry file, stored at plugins/<vendor>/<package>.json. An entry is a hand-maintained POINTER plus curation metadata: it says where a plugin lives, who wrote it, how it is licensed, and how far Signals has reviewed it. It deliberately carries no version or capability data — CI resolves the highest SemVer git tag in the entry's source repo, reads that tag's signals.yaml, validates it against the framework manifest schema (https://docs.signals.rent/schemas/signals-plugin-manifest.v1.json) and merges the result into index.json as a generated `latest` block. Beyond this schema, CI enforces: (a) the file path segments must equal the `package` field, so acme/booking-reminders lives at plugins/acme/booking-reminders.json; (b) `package` must be unique across the registry; (c) enrichment must succeed at least once for the entry to show version data in the index.

package.description: Composer package name in vendor/name form, identical to the `package` field of the plugin's signals.yaml. CI additionally enforces that this value matches the entry's own file path (plugins/<vendor>/<name>.json) and is unique across the registry; a mismatch between this value and the manifest found at the resolved tag fails enrichment for the entry.

source.description: Where the plugin's code lives. Installation is git-repository-plus-tag only: the framework clones or downloads the tagged release CI resolved, so the repository must be publicly readable over HTTPS and must publish SemVer git tags.

type.description: Install source kind. Only git repositories are supported in v1.

url.description: Public HTTPS clone URL of the plugin repository (e.g. https://github.com/acme/signals-booking-reminders.git). SSH and git:// URLs are rejected: CI clones anonymously and the framework must be able to fetch the same URL without credentials.

description.description: One-sentence summary of what the plugin does, shown in registry listings and search. Written by the entry author — the signals.yaml manifest has no description field, so this is the only source of it.

tier.description: Curation tier. `verified` means Signals reviewed a specific tagged release of this plugin (recorded in `verification`) and is required to carry a `verification` block. `community` means the plugin is listed but unreviewed: it is self-hosted only and installed entirely at the operator's own risk; community entries must not carry a `verification` block.

license.description: SPDX licence identifier for the plugin's own code (e.g. MIT, Apache-2.0, GPL-3.0-or-later, or a proprietary marker such as LicenseRef-Acme-Commercial). Informational only: listing a plugin in this registry does not change or grant any licence.

authors.description: People or organisations responsible for the plugin, for attribution and contact in listings.

url.description: Optional author homepage or profile URL (https).

homepage.description: Optional HTTPS URL for the plugin's documentation or product page, linked from the registry UI. Omit when the source repository is the only home.

keywords.description: Optional kebab-case tags used for filtering and search in the registry UI (e.g. payments, accounting, field-service). Keep them short and conventional so similar plugins cluster together.

items.description: A single kebab-case keyword: lowercase letters and digits, hyphen-separated.

status.description: Lifecycle state of the listing. Treated as "active" when absent. `deprecated` keeps the plugin installable but badges it as no longer recommended; `yanked` marks it as withdrawn — yanked entries deliberately stay in the index so consumers holding a cached copy still learn the status, and the registry UI hides them by default.

status_reason.description: Short human-readable explanation shown alongside a deprecated or yanked badge (e.g. "superseded by acme/payments-v2", "upstream API withdrawn"). Ignored when status is active or absent.

verification.description: Record of the Signals review that granted verified tier. Required when tier is "verified" and forbidden otherwise. Verification is anchored to one release: a later tag published by the plugin author is NOT automatically verified, so `latest.version` in the index may be ahead of `reviewed_version`. Consumers that require a reviewed build should compare the two.

reviewed_version.description: The exact plugin version Signals reviewed, matching the `version` field of the signals.yaml at the reviewed tag. Strict SemVer 2.0.0, as required by the manifest schema.

reviewed_at.description: Date the review completed, as YYYY-MM-DD.

added_at.description: Date this entry was first accepted into the registry, as YYYY-MM-DD. Informational; used to sort "recently added" views.
